# ts_rs - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/ts-rs/^11.1/

## Expand description

#

ts-rs

Generate typescript type declarations from rust types

[§](https://docs.rs#why)Why?

When building a web application in rust, data structures have to be shared between backend and frontend. Using this library, you can easily generate TypeScript bindings to your rust structs & enums so that you can keep your types in one place.

ts-rs might also come in handy when working with webassembly.

[§](https://docs.rs#how)How?

ts-rs exposes a single trait, `TS`. Using a derive macro, you can implement this interface for your types.
Then, you can use this trait to obtain the TypeScript bindings.
We recommend doing this in your tests.
[See the example](https://github.com/Aleph-Alpha/ts-rs/blob/main/example/src/lib.rs) and [the docs](https://docs.rs/ts-rs/latest/ts_rs/).

[§](https://docs.rs#get-started)Get started

```
[dependencies]
ts-rs = "11.1"
```
```
use ts_rs::TS;
#[derive(TS)]
#[ts(export)]
struct User {
    user_id: i32,
    first_name: String,
    last_name: String,
}
```
When running `cargo test` or `cargo test export_bindings`, the TypeScript bindings will be exported to the file `bindings/User.ts`
and will contain the following code:

`export type User = { user_id: number, first_name: string, last_name: string, };`[§](https://docs.rs#features)Features

- generate type declarations from rust structs
- generate union declarations from rust enums
- inline types
- flatten structs/types
- generate necessary imports when exporting to multiple files
- serde compatibility
- generic types
- support for ESM imports

[§](https://docs.rs#cargo-features)cargo features

| Feature | Description |
|---|---|
| serde-compat | Enabled by defaultSee the “serde compatibility”section below for more information. |
| format | Enables formatting of the generated TypeScript bindings. Currently, this unfortunately adds quite a few dependencies. |
| no-serde-warnings | By default, warnings are printed during build if unsupported serde attributes are encountered. Enabling this feature silences these warnings. |
| serde-json-impl | Implement `TS`for types fromserde_json |
| chrono-impl | Implement `TS`for types fromchrono |
| bigdecimal-impl | Implement `TS`for types frombigdecimal |
| url-impl | Implement `TS`for types fromurl |
| uuid-impl | Implement `TS`for types fromuuid |
| bson-uuid-impl | Implement `TS`forbson::oid::ObjectIdandbson::uuid |
| bytes-impl | Implement `TS`for types frombytes |
| indexmap-impl | Implement `TS`for types fromindexmap |
| ordered-float-impl | Implement `TS`for types fromordered_float |
| heapless-impl | Implement `TS`for types fromheapless |
| semver-impl | Implement `TS`for types fromsemver |
| smol_str-impl | Implement `TS`for types fromsmol_str |
| tokio-impl | Implement `TS`for types fromtokio |

If there’s a type you’re dealing with which doesn’t implement `TS`, use either
`#[ts(as = "..")]` or `#[ts(type = "..")]`, or open a PR.

[§](https://docs.rs#serde-compatability)`serde` compatability

With the `serde-compat` feature (enabled by default), serde attributes can be parsed for enums and structs.
Supported serde attributes:

- `rename`
- `rename-all`
- `rename-all-fields`
- `tag`
- `content`
- `untagged`
- `skip`
- `skip_serializing`
- `skip_serializing_if`
- `flatten`
- `default`

Note: `skip_serializing` and `skip_serializing_if` only have an effect when used together with
`#[serde(default)]`.

Note: `skip_deserializing` is ignored. If you wish to exclude a field
from the generated type, but cannot use `#[serde(skip)]`, use `#[ts(skip)]` instead.

When ts-rs encounters an unsupported serde attribute, a warning is emitted, unless the feature `no-serde-warnings` is enabled.

[§](https://docs.rs#contributing)Contributing

Contributions are always welcome!
Feel free to open an issue, discuss using GitHub discussions or open a PR.
[See CONTRIBUTING.md](https://github.com/Aleph-Alpha/ts-rs/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)

[§](https://docs.rs#msrv)MSRV

The Minimum Supported Rust Version for this crate is 1.88.0

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Dependency](https://docs.rs/struct.Dependency.html)
- A typescript type which is depended upon by other types. This information is required for generating the correct import statements.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Export](https://docs.rs/enum.ExportError.html)- Error
- An error which may occur when exporting a type

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [TS](https://docs.rs/trait.TS.html)
- A type which can be represented in TypeScript.
 Most of the time, you’d want to derive this trait instead of implementing it manually.
 ts-rs comes with implementations for all primitives, most collections, tuples, arrays and containers.
- [Type](https://docs.rs/trait.TypeVisitor.html)- Visitor
- A visitor used to iterate over all dependencies or generics of a type.
When an instance of `TypeVisitor``TS::visit_dependencies``TS::visit_generics``TypeVisitor::visit`

# parking_lot - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/parking_lot/^0.12/

## Expand description

This library provides implementations of `Mutex`, `RwLock`, `Condvar` and
`Once` that are smaller, faster and more flexible than those in the Rust
standard library. It also provides a `ReentrantMutex` type.

## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use ::`- [lock_api](https://docs.rs/lock_api/0.4.14/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/lock_api/index.html);

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [deadlock](https://docs.rs/deadlock/index.html)
- [Experimental] Deadlock detection

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [ArcMutex](https://docs.rs/struct.ArcMutexGuard.html)- Guard
- An RAII mutex guard returned by the `Arc`locking operations on`Mutex`.
- [ArcReentrant](https://docs.rs/struct.ArcReentrantMutexGuard.html)- Mutex - Guard
- An RAII mutex guard returned by the `Arc`locking operations on`ReentrantMutex`.
- [ArcRw](https://docs.rs/struct.ArcRwLockReadGuard.html)- Lock - Read - Guard
- An RAII rwlock guard returned by the `Arc`locking operations on`RwLock`.
- [ArcRw](https://docs.rs/struct.ArcRwLockUpgradableReadGuard.html)- Lock - Upgradable - Read - Guard
- An RAII rwlock guard returned by the `Arc`locking operations on`RwLock`. This is similar to the`RwLockUpgradableReadGuard`struct, except instead of using a reference to unlock the`RwLock`it uses an`Arc<RwLock>`. This has several advantages, most notably that it has an`'static`lifetime.
- [ArcRw](https://docs.rs/struct.ArcRwLockWriteGuard.html)- Lock - Write - Guard
- An RAII rwlock guard returned by the `Arc`locking operations on`RwLock`. This is similar to the`RwLockWriteGuard`struct, except instead of using a reference to unlock the`RwLock`it uses an`Arc<RwLock>`. This has several advantages, most notably that it has an`'static`lifetime.
- [Condvar](https://docs.rs/struct.Condvar.html)
- A Condition Variable
- [Once](https://docs.rs/struct.Once.html)
- A synchronization primitive which can be used to run a one-time initialization. Useful for one-time initialization for globals, FFI or related functionality.
- [RawFair](https://docs.rs/struct.RawFairMutex.html)- Mutex
- Raw fair mutex type backed by the parking lot.
- [RawMutex](https://docs.rs/struct.RawMutex.html)
- Raw mutex type backed by the parking lot.
- [RawRw](https://docs.rs/struct.RawRwLock.html)- Lock
- Raw reader-writer lock type backed by the parking lot.
- [RawThread](https://docs.rs/struct.RawThreadId.html)- Id
- Implementation of the `GetThreadId`trait for`lock_api::ReentrantMutex`.
- [Wait](https://docs.rs/struct.WaitTimeoutResult.html)- Timeout - Result
- A type indicating whether a timed wait on a condition variable returned due to a time out or not.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Once](https://docs.rs/enum.OnceState.html)- State
- Current state of a `Once`.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [const_](https://docs.rs/fn.const_fair_mutex.html)- fair_ - mutex
- Creates a new fair mutex in an unlocked state ready for use.
- [const_](https://docs.rs/fn.const_mutex.html)- mutex
- Creates a new mutex in an unlocked state ready for use.
- [const_](https://docs.rs/fn.const_reentrant_mutex.html)- reentrant_ - mutex
- Creates a new reentrant mutex in an unlocked state ready for use.
- [const_](https://docs.rs/fn.const_rwlock.html)- rwlock
- Creates a new instance of an `RwLock<T>`which is unlocked.

## Type Aliases[§](https://docs.rs#types)

- [Fair](https://docs.rs/type.FairMutex.html)- Mutex
- A mutual exclusive primitive that is always fair, useful for protecting shared data
- [Fair](https://docs.rs/type.FairMutexGuard.html)- Mutex - Guard
- An RAII implementation of a “scoped lock” of a mutex. When this structure is dropped (falls out of scope), the lock will be unlocked.
- [Mapped](https://docs.rs/type.MappedFairMutexGuard.html)- Fair - Mutex - Guard
- An RAII mutex guard returned by `FairMutexGuard::map`, which can point to a subfield of the protected data.
- [Mapped](https://docs.rs/type.MappedMutexGuard.html)- Mutex - Guard
- An RAII mutex guard returned by `MutexGuard::map`, which can point to a subfield of the protected data.
- [Mapped](https://docs.rs/type.MappedReentrantMutexGuard.html)- Reentrant - Mutex - Guard
- An RAII mutex guard returned by `ReentrantMutexGuard::map`, which can point to a subfield of the protected data.
- [Mapped](https://docs.rs/type.MappedRwLockReadGuard.html)- RwLock - Read - Guard
- An RAII read lock guard returned by `RwLockReadGuard::map`, which can point to a subfield of the protected data.
- [Mapped](https://docs.rs/type.MappedRwLockWriteGuard.html)- RwLock - Write - Guard
- An RAII write lock guard returned by `RwLockWriteGuard::map`, which can point to a subfield of the protected data.
- [Mutex](https://docs.rs/type.Mutex.html)
- A mutual exclusion primitive useful for protecting shared data
- [Mutex](https://docs.rs/type.MutexGuard.html)- Guard
- An RAII implementation of a “scoped lock” of a mutex. When this structure is dropped (falls out of scope), the lock will be unlocked.
- [Reentrant](https://docs.rs/type.ReentrantMutex.html)- Mutex
- A mutex which can be recursively locked by a single thread.
- [Reentrant](https://docs.rs/type.ReentrantMutexGuard.html)- Mutex - Guard
- An RAII implementation of a “scoped lock” of a reentrant mutex. When this structure is dropped (falls out of scope), the lock will be unlocked.
- [RwLock](https://docs.rs/type.RwLock.html)
- A reader-writer lock
- [RwLock](https://docs.rs/type.RwLockReadGuard.html)- Read - Guard
- RAII structure used to release the shared read access of a lock when dropped.
- [RwLock](https://docs.rs/type.RwLockUpgradableReadGuard.html)- Upgradable - Read - Guard
- RAII structure used to release the upgradable read access of a lock when dropped.
- [RwLock](https://docs.rs/type.RwLockWriteGuard.html)- Write - Guard
- RAII structure used to release the exclusive write access of a lock when dropped.

# tokio - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/tokio/^1/

## Expand description

A runtime for writing reliable network applications without compromising speed.

Tokio is an event-driven, non-blocking I/O platform for writing asynchronous applications with the Rust programming language. At a high level, it provides a few major components:

- Tools for [working with asynchronous tasks](https://docs.rs#working-with-tasks), including[synchronization primitives and channels](https://docs.rs/sync/index.html)and[timeouts, sleeps, and intervals](https://docs.rs/time/index.html).
- APIs for [performing asynchronous I/O](https://docs.rs#asynchronous-io), including[TCP and UDP](https://docs.rs/net/index.html)sockets,[filesystem](https://docs.rs/fs/index.html)operations, and[process](https://docs.rs/process/index.html)and[signal](https://docs.rs/signal/index.html)management.
- A [runtime](https://docs.rs/runtime/index.html)for executing asynchronous code, including a task scheduler, an I/O driver backed by the operating system’s event queue (`epoll`,`kqueue`,`IOCP`, etc…), and a high performance timer.

Guide level documentation is found on the [website](https://tokio.rs/tokio/tutorial).

[§](https://docs.rs#a-tour-of-tokio)A Tour of Tokio

Tokio consists of a number of modules that provide a range of functionality essential for implementing asynchronous applications in Rust. In this section, we will take a brief tour of Tokio, summarizing the major APIs and their uses.

The easiest way to get started is to enable all features. Do this by
enabling the `full` feature flag:

`tokio = { version = "1", features = ["full"] }`[§](https://docs.rs#authoring-applications)Authoring applications

Tokio is great for writing applications and most users in this case shouldn’t
worry too much about what features they should pick. If you’re unsure, we suggest
going with `full` to ensure that you don’t run into any road blocks while you’re
building your application.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

This example shows the quickest way to get started with Tokio.

`tokio = { version = "1", features = ["full"] }`[§](https://docs.rs#authoring-libraries)Authoring libraries

As a library author your goal should be to provide the lightest weight crate that is based on Tokio. To achieve this you should ensure that you only enable the features you need. This allows users to pick up your crate without having to enable unnecessary features.

[§](https://docs.rs#example-1)Example

This example shows how you may want to import features for a library that just
needs to `tokio::spawn` and use a `TcpStream`.

`tokio = { version = "1", features = ["rt", "net"] }`[§](https://docs.rs#working-with-tasks)Working With Tasks

Asynchronous programs in Rust are based around lightweight, non-blocking
units of execution called [ tasks](https://docs.rs#working-with-tasks). The

[module provides important tools for working with tasks:](https://docs.rs/task/index.html)

`tokio::task`- The `spawn``JoinHandle`
- Functions for [running blocking operations](https://docs.rs/task/index.html#blocking-and-yielding)in an asynchronous task context.

The [ tokio::task](https://docs.rs/task/index.html) module is present only when the “rt” feature flag
is enabled.

The [ tokio::sync](https://docs.rs/sync/index.html) module contains synchronization primitives to use when
needing to communicate or share data. These include:

- channels (`oneshot``mpsc``watch``broadcast`
- a non-blocking `Mutex`
- an asynchronous `Barrier`

The `tokio::sync` module is present only when the “sync” feature flag is
enabled.

The [ tokio::time](https://docs.rs/time/index.html) module provides utilities for tracking time and
scheduling work. This includes functions for setting

[timeouts](https://docs.rs/time/fn.timeout.html)for tasks,

[sleeping](https://docs.rs/time/fn.sleep.html)work to run in the future, or

[repeating an operation at an interval](https://docs.rs/time/fn.interval.html).

In order to use `tokio::time`, the “time” feature flag must be enabled.

Finally, Tokio provides a *runtime* for executing asynchronous tasks. Most
applications can use the [ #[tokio::main]](https://docs.rs/attr.main.html) macro to run their code on the
Tokio runtime. However, this macro provides only basic configuration options. As
an alternative, the

[module provides more powerful APIs for configuring and managing runtimes. You should use that module if the](https://docs.rs/runtime/index.html)

`tokio::runtime``#[tokio::main]` macro doesn’t
provide the functionality you need.Using the runtime requires the “rt” or “rt-multi-thread” feature flags, to
enable the current-thread [single-threaded scheduler](https://docs.rs/runtime/index.html#current-thread-scheduler) and the [multi-thread
scheduler](https://docs.rs/runtime/index.html#multi-thread-scheduler), respectively. See the [ runtime module
documentation](https://docs.rs/runtime/index.html#runtime-scheduler) for details. In addition, the “macros” feature
flag enables the

`#[tokio::main]` and `#[tokio::test]` attributes.[§](https://docs.rs#cpu-bound-tasks-and-blocking-code)CPU-bound tasks and blocking code

Tokio is able to concurrently run many tasks on a few threads by repeatedly
swapping the currently running task on each thread. However, this kind of
swapping can only happen at `.await` points, so code that spends a long time
without reaching an `.await` will prevent other tasks from running. To
combat this, Tokio provides two kinds of threads: Core threads and blocking threads.

The core threads are where all asynchronous code runs, and Tokio will by default
spawn one for each CPU core. You can use the environment variable `TOKIO_WORKER_THREADS`
to override the default value.

The blocking threads are spawned on demand, can be used to run blocking code
that would otherwise block other tasks from running and are kept alive when
not used for a certain amount of time which can be configured with [ thread_keep_alive](https://docs.rs/runtime/struct.Builder.html#method.thread_keep_alive).
Since it is not possible for Tokio to swap out blocking tasks, like it
can do with asynchronous code, the upper limit on the number of blocking
threads is very large. These limits can be configured on the

[.](https://docs.rs/runtime/struct.Builder.html)

`Builder`To spawn a blocking task, you should use the [ spawn_blocking](https://docs.rs/task/fn.spawn_blocking.html) function.

```
#[tokio::main]
async fn main() {
    // This is running on a core thread.
    let blocking_task = tokio::task::spawn_blocking(|| {
        // This is running on a blocking thread.
        // Blocking here is ok.
    });
    // We can wait for the blocking task like this:
    // If the blocking task panics, the unwrap below will propagate the
    // panic.
    blocking_task.await.unwrap();
}
```
If your code is CPU-bound and you wish to limit the number of threads used
to run it, you should use a separate thread pool dedicated to CPU bound tasks.
For example, you could consider using the [rayon](https://docs.rs/rayon) library for CPU-bound
tasks. It is also possible to create an extra Tokio runtime dedicated to
CPU-bound tasks, but if you do this, you should be careful that the extra
runtime runs *only* CPU-bound tasks, as IO-bound tasks on that runtime
will behave poorly.

Hint: If using rayon, you can use a [ oneshot](https://docs.rs/sync/oneshot/index.html) channel to send the result back
to Tokio when the rayon task finishes.

[§](https://docs.rs#asynchronous-io)Asynchronous IO

As well as scheduling and running tasks, Tokio provides everything you need to perform input and output asynchronously.

The [ tokio::io](https://docs.rs/io/index.html) module provides Tokio’s asynchronous core I/O primitives,
the

[,](https://docs.rs/io/trait.AsyncRead.html)

`AsyncRead`[, and](https://docs.rs/io/trait.AsyncWrite.html)

`AsyncWrite`[traits. In addition, when the “io-util” feature flag is enabled, it also provides combinators and functions for working with these traits, forming as an asynchronous counterpart to](https://docs.rs/io/trait.AsyncBufRead.html)

`AsyncBufRead`[.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/io/index.html)

`std::io`Tokio also includes APIs for performing various kinds of I/O and interacting with the operating system asynchronously. These include:

- `tokio::net`- [TCP](https://docs.rs/net/tcp/index.html),- [UDP](https://docs.rs/net/struct.UdpSocket.html), and- [Unix Domain Sockets](https://docs.rs/net/unix/index.html)(enabled by the “net” feature flag),
- `tokio::fs`- `std::fs`
- `tokio::signal`
- `tokio::process`

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

A simple TCP echo server:

```
use tokio::net::TcpListener;
use tokio::io::{AsyncReadExt, AsyncWriteExt};
#[tokio::main]
async fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
    let listener = TcpListener::bind("127.0.0.1:8080").await?;
    loop {
        let (mut socket, _) = listener.accept().await?;
        tokio::spawn(async move {
            let mut buf = [0; 1024];
            // In a loop, read data from the socket and write the data back.
            loop {
                let n = match socket.read(&mut buf).await {
                    // socket closed
                    Ok(0) => return,
                    Ok(n) => n,
                    Err(e) => {
                        eprintln!("failed to read from socket; err = {:?}", e);
                        return;
                    }
                };
                // Write the data back
                if let Err(e) = socket.write_all(&buf[0..n]).await {
                    eprintln!("failed to write to socket; err = {:?}", e);
                    return;
                }
            }
        });
    }
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#feature-flags)Feature flags

Tokio uses a set of [feature flags](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/manifest.html#the-features-section) to reduce the amount of compiled code. It
is possible to just enable certain features over others. By default, Tokio
does not enable any features but allows one to enable a subset for their use
case. Below is a list of the available feature flags. You may also notice
above each function, struct and trait there is listed one or more feature flags
that are required for that item to be used. If you are new to Tokio it is
recommended that you use the `full` feature flag which will enable all public APIs.
Beware though that this will pull in many extra dependencies that you may not
need.

- `full`: Enables all features listed below except- `test-util`and unstable features.
- `rt`: Enables- `tokio::spawn`, the current-thread scheduler, and non-scheduler utilities.
- `rt-multi-thread`: Enables the heavier, multi-threaded, work-stealing scheduler.
- `io-util`: Enables the IO based- `Ext`traits.
- `io-std`: Enable- `Stdout`,- `Stdin`and- `Stderr`types.
- `net`: Enables- `tokio::net`types such as- `TcpStream`,- `UnixStream`and- `UdpSocket`, as well as (on Unix-like systems)- `AsyncFd`and (on FreeBSD)- `PollAio`.
- `time`: Enables- `tokio::time`types and allows the schedulers to enable the built-in timer.
- `process`: Enables- `tokio::process`types.
- `macros`: Enables- `#[tokio::main]`and- `#[tokio::test]`macros.
- `sync`: Enables all- `tokio::sync`types.
- `signal`: Enables all- `tokio::signal`types.
- `fs`: Enables- `tokio::fs`types.
- `test-util`: Enables testing based infrastructure for the Tokio runtime.
- `parking_lot`: As a potential optimization, use the- `parking_lot`- `const`context.- `MSRV`may increase according to the- `parking_lot`

*Note:  AsyncRead and AsyncWrite traits do not require any features and are
always available.*

[§](https://docs.rs#unstable-features)Unstable features

Some feature flags are only available when specifying the `tokio_unstable` flag:

- `tracing`: Enables tracing events.
- `io-uring`: Enables- `io-uring`(Linux only).
- `taskdump`: Enables- `taskdump`(Linux only).

Likewise, this flag enables access to unstable APIs.

This flag enables **unstable** features. The public API of these features
may break in 1.x releases. To enable these features, the `--cfg tokio_unstable` argument must be passed to `rustc` when compiling. This
serves to explicitly opt-in to features which may break semver conventions,
since Cargo [does not yet directly support such opt-ins](https://internals.rust-lang.org/t/feature-request-unstable-opt-in-non-transitive-crate-features/16193#why-not-a-crate-feature-2).

You can specify it in your project’s `.cargo/config.toml` file:

```
[build]
rustflags = ["--cfg", "tokio_unstable"]
```
`[build]` section does **not**go in a

`Cargo.toml` file. Instead it must be placed in the Cargo config
file `.cargo/config.toml`.
Alternatively, you can specify it with an environment variable:

```
## Many *nix shells:
export RUSTFLAGS="--cfg tokio_unstable"
cargo build
```
```
## Windows PowerShell:
$Env:RUSTFLAGS="--cfg tokio_unstable"
cargo build
```
[§](https://docs.rs#supported-platforms)Supported platforms

Tokio currently guarantees support for the following platforms:

- Linux
- Windows
- Android (API level 21)
- macOS
- iOS
- FreeBSD

Tokio will continue to support these platforms in the future. However, future releases may change requirements such as the minimum required libc version on Linux, the API level on Android, or the supported FreeBSD release.

Beyond the above platforms, Tokio is intended to work on all platforms
supported by the mio crate. You can find a longer list [in mio’s
documentation](https://crates.io/crates/mio#platforms). However, these additional platforms may
become unsupported in the future.

Note that Wine is considered to be a different platform from Windows. See mio’s documentation for more information on Wine support.

[§](https://docs.rs#wasm-support)`WASM` support

Tokio has some limited support for the `WASM` platform. Without the
`tokio_unstable` flag, the following features are supported:

- `sync`
- `macros`
- `io-util`
- `rt`
- `time`

Enabling any other feature (including `full`) will cause a compilation
failure.

The `time` module will only work on `WASM` platforms that have support for
timers (e.g. wasm32-wasi). The timing functions will panic if used on a `WASM`
platform that does not support timers.

Note also that if the runtime becomes indefinitely idle, it will panic immediately instead of blocking forever. On platforms that don’t support time, this means that the runtime can never be idle in any way.

[§](https://docs.rs#unstable-wasm-support)Unstable `WASM` support

Tokio also has unstable support for some additional `WASM` features. This
requires the use of the `tokio_unstable` flag.

Using this flag enables the use of `tokio::net` on the wasm32-wasi target.
However, not all methods are available on the networking types as `WASI`
currently does not support the creation of new sockets from within `WASM`.
Because of this, sockets must currently be created via the `FromRawFd`
trait.

## Macros[§](https://docs.rs#macros)

- [join](https://docs.rs/macro.join.html)- `macros`
- Waits on multiple concurrent branches, returning when **all**branches complete.
- [pin](https://docs.rs/macro.pin.html)
- Pins a value on the stack.
- [select](https://docs.rs/macro.select.html)- `macros`
- Waits on multiple concurrent branches, returning when the **first**branch completes, cancelling the remaining branches.
- [task_](https://docs.rs/macro.task_local.html)- local - `rt`
- Declares a new task-local key of type `tokio::task::LocalKey`
- [try_](https://docs.rs/macro.try_join.html)- join - `macros`
- Waits on multiple concurrent branches, returning when **all**branches complete with`Ok(_)`or on the first`Err(_)`.

## Attribute Macros[§](https://docs.rs#attributes)

- [main](https://docs.rs/attr.main.html)- `rt`and- `macros`

helps set up a `Runtime`without requiring the user to use[Runtime](https://docs.rs/tokio/runtime/struct.Runtime.html)or[Builder](https://docs.rs/tokio/runtime/struct.Builder.html)directly.

This macro helps set up a `Runtime`without requiring the user to use[Runtime](https://docs.rs/tokio/runtime/struct.Runtime.html)or[Builder](https://docs.rs/tokio/runtime/struct.Builder.html)directly.

# rship_sync - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/rship-sync/4.0.0-canary.64/target-redirect/rship_sync/

## Expand description

Sync Value System

High-precision synchronized value distribution using hyphae cells. Runs in-process with a 240Hz master clock for value updates.

[§](https://docs.rs#usage)Usage

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
use rship_sync::{context, ValueRunnerRegistry, SyncValueConfig};
use std::sync::Arc;
// Initialize (once at startup)
let registry = Arc::new(ValueRunnerRegistry::new());
context::init(registry);
// Create and watch values
rship_sync::ensure_value("my/value", &SyncValueConfig { value: 0.0, rate: 1.0, running: true }, 30.0);
let cell = rship_sync::watch_value("my/value");
```
## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use commands::`- [SetSyncValueSampleRate](https://docs.rs/commands/struct.SetSyncValueSampleRate.html);
- `pub use commands::`- [SetSyncValueValue](https://docs.rs/commands/struct.SetSyncValueValue.html);
- `pub use commands::`- [StartSyncValue](https://docs.rs/commands/struct.StartSyncValue.html);
- `pub use engine::`- [SyncValueEngine](https://docs.rs/engine/struct.SyncValueEngine.html);
- `pub use entities::`- [MASTER_HZ](https://docs.rs/entities/constant.MASTER_HZ.html);
- `pub use entities::`- [Preset](https://docs.rs/entities/enum.Preset.html);

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [clock](https://docs.rs/clock/index.html)
- High-precision master clock for synchronized value distribution.
- [commands](https://docs.rs/commands/index.html)
- Sync value commands.
- [context](https://docs.rs/context/index.html)
- Global sync context for accessing the value registry from reports.
- [engine](https://docs.rs/engine/index.html)
- `SyncValueEngine`— projects- `SyncValueRuntime`entity state into the local- `ValueRunnerRegistry`.
- [entities](https://docs.rs/entities/index.html)
- Sync-specific types.
- [heartbeat](https://docs.rs/heartbeat/index.html)
- `SyncValueHeartbeat`— periodic 1Hz re-emit of- `SetSyncValueRate`for every known- `SyncValueRuntime`entity.
- [local](https://docs.rs/local/index.html)
- Local-only sync-value mutators for callers that derive their value
deterministically per-peer from the binding-node graph (Speed, Clock,
Wave, Interval generators). These keys must NOT go through the
`EnsureSyncValue`command path — that would emit a peer-replicated`SyncValueRuntime`entity, and every peer that locally re-evaluates the same generator graph would race to upsert the same key with a different UUID, doubling/N-tupling entity counts forever.
- [reports](https://docs.rs/reports/index.html)
- Sync value reports.
- [runtime_](https://docs.rs/runtime_entity/index.html)- entity
- `SyncValueRuntime`entity — peer-replicated runtime state for a sync value.
- [value_](https://docs.rs/value_runner/index.html)- runner
- Lock-free value runner using hyphae cells.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [link](https://docs.rs/fn.link.html)
- Force linking to ensure inventory registrations are collected.

[19](https://docs.rs#19)//! ```

[33](https://docs.rs#33)// Entity types (available on all platforms for type safety)
[34](https://docs.rs#34)pub mod entities;
[35](https://docs.rs#35)// Peer-replicated runtime state entity (native-only — uses myko item
[36](https://docs.rs#36)// infrastructure that requires server-side registration machinery).
[37](https://docs.rs#37)#[cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))]
[38](https://docs.rs#38)pub mod runtime_entity;
[39](https://docs.rs#39)// Engine that mirrors SyncValueRuntime entity state into the local
[40](https://docs.rs#40)// ValueRunnerRegistry. Native-only (subscribes to server queries).
[41](https://docs.rs#41)#[cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))]
[42](https://docs.rs#42)pub mod engine;
[43](https://docs.rs#43)// Periodic 1Hz re-emit of SetSyncValueRate per entity so late-joining
[44](https://docs.rs#44)// peers converge within a second. Native-only.
[45](https://docs.rs#45)#[cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))]
[46](https://docs.rs#46)pub mod heartbeat;
[47](https://docs.rs#47)

[50](https://docs.rs#50)#[cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))]

[52](https://docs.rs#52)    DestroySyncValue, EnsureSyncValue, PauseSyncValue, ResetSyncValue, SetSyncValueRate,

[66](https://docs.rs#66)
[67](https://docs.rs#67)// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
[68](https://docs.rs#68)// Local-only sync-value helpers (no entity emission, no replication).
[69](https://docs.rs#69)// ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
[70](https://docs.rs#70)
[71](https://docs.rs#71)/// Local-only sync-value mutators for callers that derive their value
[72](https://docs.rs#72)/// deterministically per-peer from the binding-node graph (Speed, Clock,
[73](https://docs.rs#73)/// Wave, Interval generators). These keys must NOT go through the
[74](https://docs.rs#74)/// `EnsureSyncValue` command path — that would emit a peer-replicated
[75](https://docs.rs#75)/// `SyncValueRuntime` entity, and every peer that locally re-evaluates
[76](https://docs.rs#76)/// the same generator graph would race to upsert the same key with a
[77](https://docs.rs#77)/// different UUID, doubling/N-tupling entity counts forever.
[78](https://docs.rs#78)///
[79](https://docs.rs#79)/// External-input-driven sync values (UI scrubs, control panels) should
[80](https://docs.rs#80)/// continue to use the command path so their state replicates.
[81](https://docs.rs#81)#[cfg(not(target_arch = "wasm32"))]
[82](https://docs.rs#82)pub mod local {
[83](https://docs.rs#83)    use std::sync::Arc;
[84](https://docs.rs#84)
[85](https://docs.rs#85)    use crate::{context, entities::SyncValueConfig};
[86](https://docs.rs#86)
[87](https://docs.rs#87)    /// Ensure a runner exists for `key`, applying `config` only if we're
[88](https://docs.rs#88)    /// creating it. If the runner already exists, its value/rate/running
[89](https://docs.rs#89)    /// state is preserved — callers that need to reset those must do so
[90](https://docs.rs#90)    /// explicitly via `set_value` / `set_rate` / `start` / `pause`. This
[91](https://docs.rs#91)    /// matters for generator nodes (Speed, Wave, Clock) whose `make_cell`
[92](https://docs.rs#92)    /// re-runs when the reactive cell is rebuilt on new subscriptions;
[93](https://docs.rs#93)    /// overwriting `value` would reset accumulated position every time.
[94](https://docs.rs#94)    pub fn ensure_value(key: impl Into<Arc<str>>, config: &SyncValueConfig, sample_rate: f64) {
[95](https://docs.rs#95)        let key = key.into();
[96](https://docs.rs#96)        let registry = context::registry();
[97](https://docs.rs#97)        registry.get_or_create_with_config(key.clone(), config);
[98](https://docs.rs#98)        let cell = context::samplerate_cell(key, sample_rate);
[99](https://docs.rs#99)        hyphae::Mutable::set(&cell, sample_rate);
[100](https://docs.rs#100)    }
[101](https://docs.rs#101)
[102](https://docs.rs#102)    /// Update the rate of an existing local runner. No-op if missing.
[103](https://docs.rs#103)    pub fn set_rate(key: &str, rate: f64) {
[104](https://docs.rs#104)        if let Some(runner) = context::registry().get(key) {
[105](https://docs.rs#105)            runner.set_rate(rate);
[106](https://docs.rs#106)        }
[107](https://docs.rs#107)    }
[108](https://docs.rs#108)
[109](https://docs.rs#109)    /// Update the value of an existing local runner. No-op if missing.
[110](https://docs.rs#110)    pub fn set_value(key: &str, value: f64) {
[111](https://docs.rs#111)        if let Some(runner) = context::registry().get(key) {
[112](https://docs.rs#112)            runner.set_value(value);
[113](https://docs.rs#113)        }
[114](https://docs.rs#114)    }
[115](https://docs.rs#115)
[116](https://docs.rs#116)    /// Resume an existing local runner. No-op if missing.
[117](https://docs.rs#117)    pub fn start(key: &str) {
[118](https://docs.rs#118)        if let Some(runner) = context::registry().get(key) {
[119](https://docs.rs#119)            runner.start();
[120](https://docs.rs#120)        }
[121](https://docs.rs#121)    }
[122](https://docs.rs#122)
[123](https://docs.rs#123)    /// Pause an existing local runner. No-op if missing.
[124](https://docs.rs#124)    pub fn pause(key: &str) {
[125](https://docs.rs#125)        if let Some(runner) = context::registry().get(key) {
[126](https://docs.rs#126)            runner.pause();
[127](https://docs.rs#127)        }
[128](https://docs.rs#128)    }
[129](https://docs.rs#129)
[130](https://docs.rs#130)    /// Update the subscriber sample rate. No-op if the samplerate cell
[131](https://docs.rs#131)    /// for this key was never created (i.e. nobody called `ensure_value`).
[132](https://docs.rs#132)    pub fn set_sample_rate(key: &str, hz: f64) {
[133](https://docs.rs#133)        let _ = context::set_samplerate(key, hz);
[134](https://docs.rs#134)    }
[135](https://docs.rs#135)
[136](https://docs.rs#136)    /// Remove a local runner. No-op if missing.
[137](https://docs.rs#137)    pub fn destroy(key: &str) {
[138](https://docs.rs#138)        if let Some(reg) = context::try_registry() {
[139](https://docs.rs#139)            reg.remove(key);
[140](https://docs.rs#140)        }
[141](https://docs.rs#141)    }
[142](https://docs.rs#142)}
[143](https://docs.rs#143)
[144](https://docs.rs#144)/// Force linking to ensure inventory registrations are collected.
[145](https://docs.rs#145)pub fn link() {}

# MasterClock in rship_sync::clock - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/rship-sync/4.0.0-canary.64/rship_sync/clock/struct.MasterClock.html

`pub struct MasterClock { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

Master clock that drives all synchronized values.

Runs at 240 Hz using hyphae’s high-precision interval.

## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

    &self,
    preset: [Preset](https://docs.rs/entities/enum.Preset.html),

#### pub fn [cell_at_preset](https://docs.rs#method.cell_at_preset)(
    &self,
    preset: [Preset](https://docs.rs/entities/enum.Preset.html),
) -> [Cell](https://docs.rs/hyphae/1.1.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/hyphae/cell/struct.Cell.html)<[Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[ClockTick](https://docs.rs/struct.ClockTick.html)>, [CellImmutable](https://docs.rs/hyphae/1.1.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/hyphae/cell/struct.CellImmutable.html)>

Create a filtered cell that only emits at the given preset rate.

Returns `Cell<Option<ClockTick>, _>` because the filter starts empty —
the cell holds `None` until the first tick that satisfies the divisor
passes the predicate.

# EnsureSyncValue in rship_sync::commands - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/rship-sync/4.0.0-canary.64/rship_sync/commands/struct.EnsureSyncValue.html

```
pub struct EnsureSyncValue {
    pub key:
```
[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html),
    pub config: [SyncValueConfig](https://docs.rs/entities/struct.SyncValueConfig.html),
    pub sample_rate: [f64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.f64.html),
}## Expand description

Ensure a sync value exists. Idempotent on existing entities — does
NOT overwrite anchor/rate/running when the entity already exists for
this key. Callers that need a forced reset (e.g. animator Start)
dispatch explicit `SetSyncValueValue` / `SetSyncValueRate` /
`Pause|StartSyncValue` follow-ups.

This semantic is what lets every peer’s generator handler dispatch EnsureSyncValue redundantly without fighting — the first arrival establishes the anchor, every subsequent arrival on every peer is a no-op. Combined with deterministic UUID-from-key derivation, simultaneous creates from multiple peers merge into one entity.

## Fields[§](https://docs.rs#fields)

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.key)

`key: `[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)The value key

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.config)

`config: `[SyncValueConfig](https://docs.rs/entities/struct.SyncValueConfig.html)Value configuration (value, rate, running) — applied only on first
creation; ignored if an entity already exists for `key`.

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.sample_rate)

`sample_rate: `[f64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.f64.html)Sample rate in Hz (updates per second sent to subscribers) — applied only on first creation.

pub struct PauseSyncValue {
    pub key:
```
[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html),
}## Expand description

Pause auto-incrementing a sync value.

Freezes the anchor at the value extrapolated to *now*, so resume
continues from exactly where playback stopped.

# ResetSyncValue in rship_sync::commands - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/rship-sync/4.0.0-canary.64/rship_sync/commands/struct.ResetSyncValue.html

```
pub struct ResetSyncValue {
    pub key:
```
[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html),
    pub config: [SyncValueConfig](https://docs.rs/entities/struct.SyncValueConfig.html),
    pub sample_rate: [f64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.f64.html),
}## Expand description

Force a sync value into a known state — unlike `EnsureSyncValue`, this
ALWAYS overwrites (value, rate, running, sample_rate). Uses the stable
UUID-from-key id so it targets the same entity whether it currently
exists or not; callers avoid the intra-transaction `find_by_key` race
that made `Ensure + Set + Set + Pause` chains flaky when the entity
was created earlier in the same tx.

## Fields[§](https://docs.rs#fields)

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.key)

`key: `[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.config)

`config: `[SyncValueConfig](https://docs.rs/entities/struct.SyncValueConfig.html)[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.sample_rate)

`sample_rate: `[f64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.f64.html)## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

# SetSyncValueRate in rship_sync::commands - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/rship-sync/4.0.0-canary.64/rship_sync/commands/struct.SetSyncValueRate.html

## Expand description

Set the rate of change for a sync value. Re-anchors at the current extrapolated value so the trajectory bends at “now” without jumping.

## Fields[§](https://docs.rs#fields)

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.key)

`key: `[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)The value key

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.rate)

`rate: `[f64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.f64.html)The new rate (value change per second)

# SetSyncValueSampleRate in rship_sync::commands - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/rship-sync/4.0.0-canary.64/rship_sync/commands/struct.SetSyncValueSampleRate.html

## Expand description

Set the subscription sample rate for a sync value (Hz).

This controls how often updates are sent to subscribers, not how fast the value changes (that’s SetSyncValueRate).

## Fields[§](https://docs.rs#fields)

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.key)

`key: `[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)The value key

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.samplerate)

`samplerate: `[f64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.f64.html)The new sample rate in Hz (updates per second)

# SetSyncValueValue in rship_sync::commands - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/rship-sync/4.0.0-canary.64/rship_sync/commands/struct.SetSyncValueValue.html

## Expand description

Set the current value of a sync value. Re-anchors at `now` so the
new value is exactly what subscribers see at the next tick.

# StartSyncValue in rship_sync::commands - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/rship-sync/4.0.0-canary.64/rship_sync/commands/struct.StartSyncValue.html

```
pub struct StartSyncValue {
    pub key:
```
[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html),
}## Expand description

Start auto-incrementing a sync value.

Re-anchors at the *paused* anchor value but stamps `anchor_time_ms`
to now so that the trajectory restarts cleanly from where it was
frozen.

## Fields[§](https://docs.rs#fields)

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.key)

`key: `[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)The value key

# Preset in rship_sync::entities - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/rship-sync/4.0.0-canary.64/rship_sync/entities/enum.Preset.html

```
pub enum Preset {
    Hz240,
    Hz120,
    Hz80,
    Hz60,
    Hz40,
    Hz30,
    Hz20,
    Hz10,
}
```
## Expand description

Preset subscription rates derived from the 240 Hz master clock.

All subscribers on the same preset receive identical ticks, ensuring perfect synchronization.

## Variants[§](https://docs.rs#variants)

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Hz240)

### Hz240

240 Hz (every tick)

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Hz120)

### Hz120

120 Hz (every 2nd tick)

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Hz80)

### Hz80

80 Hz (every 3rd tick)

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Hz60)

### Hz60

60 Hz (every 4th tick)

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Hz40)

### Hz40

40 Hz (every 6th tick)

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Hz30)

### Hz30

30 Hz (every 8th tick)

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Hz20)

### Hz20

20 Hz (every 12th tick)

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Hz10)

### Hz10

10 Hz (every 24th tick)

# SyncValueHeartbeat in rship_sync::heartbeat - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/rship-sync/4.0.0-canary.64/rship_sync/heartbeat/struct.SyncValueHeartbeat.html

`pub struct SyncValueHeartbeat { /* private fields */ }`## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/rship_sync/heartbeat.rs.html#75-99)#### pub fn [start](https://docs.rs#method.start)(ctx: [Arc](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/sync/struct.Arc.html)<[CellServerCtx](https://docs.rs/myko/4.22.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/myko/server/context/struct.CellServerCtx.html)>) -> Self

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/rship_sync/heartbeat.rs.html#75-99)

#### pub fn [start](https://docs.rs#method.start)(ctx: [Arc](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/sync/struct.Arc.html)<[CellServerCtx](https://docs.rs/myko/4.22.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/myko/server/context/struct.CellServerCtx.html)>) -> Self

Start a heartbeat for every existing and future `SyncValueRuntime`
entity. Runs for the lifetime of the returned struct — `Box::leak`
it (or own it) on the server to keep heartbeats alive.

Must be called from inside a tokio runtime context; the captured handle is used to dispatch heartbeat command execution onto the blocking thread pool so the reactive scheduler isn’t blocked.

# WatchSyncValue in rship_sync::reports - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/rship-sync/4.0.0-canary.64/rship_sync/reports/struct.WatchSyncValue.html

```
pub struct WatchSyncValue {
    pub key:
```
[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html),
}## Expand description

Report that streams sync value updates.

Uses `get_or_create` to ensure the runner exists and is held alive by the
report’s cell. Configuration (rate, running state) is applied separately
via `EnsureSyncValue` / `SetSyncValueRate`.

# SyncValueRunningState in rship_sync::runtime_entity - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/rship-sync/4.0.0-canary.64/rship_sync/runtime_entity/enum.SyncValueRunningState.html

```
pub enum SyncValueRunningState {
    Running,
    Paused,
}
```
## Expand description

Running state of a sync value. Encoded explicitly (vs. a bool) so the TS type-export reads cleanly in UI code.

## Variants[§](https://docs.rs#variants)

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Running)

### Running

Value is advancing per its rate. Any peer reading the value
computes `anchor_value + rate * (now - anchor_time)`.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Paused)

### Paused

Value is static at `anchor_value`. Rate is preserved for when the
runner is resumed.

## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

## Trait Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#trait-implementations)

# SyncValueRuntime in rship_sync::runtime_entity - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/rship-sync/4.0.0-canary.64/rship_sync/runtime_entity/struct.SyncValueRuntime.html

```
pub struct SyncValueRuntime {
    pub key:
```
[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html),
    pub anchor_value: [f64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.f64.html),
    pub anchor_time_ms: [i64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.i64.html),
    pub rate: [f64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.f64.html),
    pub running: [SyncValueRunningState](https://docs.rs/enum.SyncValueRunningState.html),
    pub sample_rate_hz: [f64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.f64.html),
    pub owner: [ServerId](https://docs.rs/myko/4.22.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/myko/entities/server/struct.ServerId.html),
    pub id: [SyncValueRuntimeId](https://docs.rs/struct.SyncValueRuntimeId.html),
}## Expand description

Replicated runtime state for a sync value — one row per value `key`.

The `key` is the external identity (e.g.
`"control-panel/animator/<control>/<session>/offset"`). The entity’s
auto-generated id is unused as a lookup key; consumers query by `key`.

## Fields[§](https://docs.rs#fields)

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.key)

`key: `[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)Stable external key. This is what consumers of the sync value reference — animator offsets, generator outputs, etc.

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.anchor_value)

`anchor_value: `[f64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.f64.html)Anchor value — the instantaneous value at `anchor_time_ms`. When
`running == Running`, the current effective value is
`anchor_value + rate * (now_ms - anchor_time_ms) / 1000`.

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.anchor_time_ms)

`anchor_time_ms: `[i64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.i64.html)Wall-clock ms since Unix epoch at which `anchor_value` was taken.
Using an explicit timestamp rather than a tick count keeps the
entity clock-source-agnostic and lets peers with NTP-synced clocks
agree on current value without a shared tick counter.

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.rate)

`rate: `[f64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.f64.html)Rate of change per second (applied only while running).

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.running)

`running: `[SyncValueRunningState](https://docs.rs/enum.SyncValueRunningState.html)Running / paused state.

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.sample_rate_hz)

`sample_rate_hz: `[f64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.f64.html)Preferred sample rate (Hz) at which subscribers should receive
updates from the local `cell_at_hz`. Separate from the master tick
rate; purely a subscriber-side concern.

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.owner)

`owner: `[ServerId](https://docs.rs/myko/4.22.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/myko/entities/server/struct.ServerId.html)Peer that currently owns tick-advance for this value. On failure, ownership transfers via a ReparentSyncValueRuntime command (TBD).

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.id)

`id: `[SyncValueRuntimeId](https://docs.rs/struct.SyncValueRuntimeId.html)## Trait Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#trait-implementations)

# ValueRunner in rship_sync::value_runner - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/rship-sync/4.0.0-canary.64/rship_sync/value_runner/struct.ValueRunner.html

`pub struct ValueRunner { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

Runner for a single synchronized value.

The runner is updated by the registry’s batch tick handler. The latest
`ValueUpdate` lives in a `parking_lot::Mutex` rather than a hyphae `Cell`
because the only consumer pattern is “sample latest value when an
interval source fires” — a `.get()` style read, not a subscribe.
`Cell<ValueUpdate>` paid arc_swap drop cost on every 240Hz write
(`Debt::pay_all` was 22% self in the latest perf trace) for thread-safety
machinery we weren’t using; an uncontended Mutex write is a single CAS.

## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

# ValueRunnerRegistry in rship_sync::value_runner - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/rship-sync/4.0.0-canary.64/rship_sync/value_runner/struct.ValueRunnerRegistry.html

`pub struct ValueRunnerRegistry { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

A collection of value runners sharing a single clock.

The registry owns the clock subscription and batch-updates all runners on each tick, avoiding per-runner subscription overhead.

Interval timers for custom Hz rates are shared across all values, ensuring synchronized sampling.

[§](https://docs.rs#manual-cleanup)Manual Cleanup

The registry holds strong references to runners. Runners must be
explicitly removed via `remove()` (called by DestroySyncValue).

High-precision master clock for synchronized value distribution.

# rship_sync::commands - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/rship-sync/4.0.0-canary.64/rship_sync/commands/index.html

## Expand description

Sync value commands.

Lifecycle: EnsureSyncValue → StartSyncValue / PauseSyncValue → DestroySyncValue Watching: WatchSyncValue report (value runner is auto-created on first watch).

Commands describe state transitions by emitting `SyncValueRuntime`
entity SET/DEL events. The engine in `crate::engine` is the single
applier — it subscribes to entity changes (peer-replicated via
`myko_server::PeerPersister`) and projects them into the local
`ValueRunnerRegistry`. This means a state change initiated on peer A
takes effect locally on A (via emit-side apply) and propagates to all
other peers via the entity event without a second round-trip.

Anchor handling: changes that affect the value trajectory (rate
change, pause, set value) re-anchor at the current wall-clock time so
`value_at(t) = anchor_value + rate * (t - anchor_time_ms) / 1000` is
continuous across peers. Resume/Start does NOT recompute the anchor —
the previous pause already froze the anchor at “now”.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Destroy](https://docs.rs/struct.DestroySyncValue.html)- Sync - Value
- Remove a sync value. Active subscribers will stop receiving updates.
- [Destroy](https://docs.rs/struct.DestroySyncValueArgs.html)- Sync - Value - Args
- [Ensure](https://docs.rs/struct.EnsureSyncValue.html)- Sync - Value
- Ensure a sync value exists. Idempotent on existing entities — does
NOT overwrite anchor/rate/running when the entity already exists for
this key. Callers that need a forced reset (e.g. animator Start)
dispatch explicit `SetSyncValueValue`/`SetSyncValueRate`/`Pause|StartSyncValue`follow-ups.
- [Ensure](https://docs.rs/struct.EnsureSyncValueArgs.html)- Sync - Value - Args
- [Pause](https://docs.rs/struct.PauseSyncValue.html)- Sync - Value
- Pause auto-incrementing a sync value.
- [Pause](https://docs.rs/struct.PauseSyncValueArgs.html)- Sync - Value - Args
- [Reset](https://docs.rs/struct.ResetSyncValue.html)- Sync - Value
- Force a sync value into a known state — unlike `EnsureSyncValue`, this ALWAYS overwrites (value, rate, running, sample_rate). Uses the stable UUID-from-key id so it targets the same entity whether it currently exists or not; callers avoid the intra-transaction`find_by_key`race that made`Ensure + Set + Set + Pause`chains flaky when the entity was created earlier in the same tx.
- [Reset](https://docs.rs/struct.ResetSyncValueArgs.html)- Sync - Value - Args
- [SetSync](https://docs.rs/struct.SetSyncValueRate.html)- Value - Rate
- Set the rate of change for a sync value. Re-anchors at the current extrapolated value so the trajectory bends at “now” without jumping.
- [SetSync](https://docs.rs/struct.SetSyncValueRateArgs.html)- Value - Rate - Args
- [SetSync](https://docs.rs/struct.SetSyncValueSampleRate.html)- Value - Sample - Rate
- Set the subscription sample rate for a sync value (Hz).
- [SetSync](https://docs.rs/struct.SetSyncValueSampleRateArgs.html)- Value - Sample - Rate - Args
- [SetSync](https://docs.rs/struct.SetSyncValueValue.html)- Value - Value
- Set the current value of a sync value. Re-anchors at `now`so the new value is exactly what subscribers see at the next tick.
- [SetSync](https://docs.rs/struct.SetSyncValueValueArgs.html)- Value - Value - Args
- [Start](https://docs.rs/struct.StartSyncValue.html)- Sync - Value
- Start auto-incrementing a sync value.
- [Start](https://docs.rs/struct.StartSyncValueArgs.html)- Sync - Value - Args

# rship_sync::engine - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/rship-sync/4.0.0-canary.64/rship_sync/engine/index.html

## Expand description

`SyncValueEngine` — projects `SyncValueRuntime` entity state into the
local `ValueRunnerRegistry`.

Each rship server runs one engine instance. The engine subscribes to all
`SyncValueRuntime` entities (which are peer-replicated via
`myko_server::PeerPersister`) and mirrors changes into the in-process
sync registry that animator/generator nodes read from.

The engine is the single applier: commands describe state changes by emitting entity SET/DEL events, and every peer’s engine applies them locally. This means a UI command on peer A immediately updates A’s registry (via local apply on emit) and, after the peer-WS hop, B’s registry too.

Tick-advance ownership is encoded on the entity (`owner: ServerId`).
Non-owner peers hold the last-known anchor and compute `value_at(now)`
from it locally — they don’t tick or emit fresh anchors. (The
per-runner tick loop in `ValueRunnerRegistry` runs on every peer; for
non-owners the rate stays at 0 unless replicated, so the runner is
effectively passive. Ownership-driven tick filtering lands in a
follow-up.)

---

# rship_sync::local - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/rship-sync/4.0.0-canary.64/rship_sync/local/index.html

## Expand description

Local-only sync-value mutators for callers that derive their value
deterministically per-peer from the binding-node graph (Speed, Clock,
Wave, Interval generators). These keys must NOT go through the
`EnsureSyncValue` command path — that would emit a peer-replicated
`SyncValueRuntime` entity, and every peer that locally re-evaluates
the same generator graph would race to upsert the same key with a
different UUID, doubling/N-tupling entity counts forever.

External-input-driven sync values (UI scrubs, control panels) should continue to use the command path so their state replicates.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [destroy](https://docs.rs/fn.destroy.html)
- Remove a local runner. No-op if missing.
- [ensure_](https://docs.rs/fn.ensure_value.html)- value
- Ensure a runner exists for `key`, applying`config`only if we’re creating it. If the runner already exists, its value/rate/running state is preserved — callers that need to reset those must do so explicitly via`set_value`/`set_rate`/`start`/`pause`. This matters for generator nodes (Speed, Wave, Clock) whose`make_cell`re-runs when the reactive cell is rebuilt on new subscriptions; overwriting`value`would reset accumulated position every time.
- [pause](https://docs.rs/fn.pause.html)
- Pause an existing local runner. No-op if missing.
- [set_](https://docs.rs/fn.set_rate.html)- rate
- Update the rate of an existing local runner. No-op if missing.
- [set_](https://docs.rs/fn.set_sample_rate.html)- sample_ - rate
- Update the subscriber sample rate. No-op if the samplerate cell
for this key was never created (i.e. nobody called `ensure_value`).
- [set_](https://docs.rs/fn.set_value.html)- value
- Update the value of an existing local runner. No-op if missing.
- [start](https://docs.rs/fn.start.html)
- Resume an existing local runner. No-op if missing.

---

# rship_sync::runtime_entity - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/rship-sync/4.0.0-canary.64/rship_sync/runtime_entity/index.html

## Expand description

`SyncValueRuntime` entity — peer-replicated runtime state for a sync value.

This entity is how sync-value state is replicated across rship cluster
members without going through sync_server. It’s stored via myko’s
`PeerPersister` (declared in `apps/server/src/main.rs`), which means:

- Emitting a `SyncValueRuntime`SET event on peer A fans the event out to every connected peer via the peer-WS mesh (no Postgres hit).
- Receiving peers apply the event to their local entity store.
- A local `SyncValueEngine`(see`engine.rs`) subscribes to entity changes and mirrors them into the peer’s local`ValueRunnerRegistry`.

Ownership is tracked via `#[server_owned] owner: ServerId`. The owner
peer is authoritative for tick-advance of the value — it computes
`value_at(now) = anchor_value + rate * (now - anchor_time)` locally
and periodically emits fresh anchors. Non-owners read the entity’s
current anchor and compute the same value locally from their own clock.

For the majority case where a value’s rate is driven by a binding-node graph (replicated deterministically to every peer), no cross-peer replication is needed per tick — each peer’s local graph writes its own local runner. The entity is updated only on user-initiated state changes (scrubs, play/pause) or low-frequency owner-driven anchor refreshes.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Count](https://docs.rs/struct.CountAllSyncValueRuntimes.html)- AllSync - Value - Runtimes
- [Count](https://docs.rs/struct.CountSyncValueRuntimes.html)- Sync - Value - Runtimes
- [Delete](https://docs.rs/struct.DeleteSyncValueRuntime.html)- Sync - Value - Runtime
- Command to delete a single entity by ID
- [Delete](https://docs.rs/struct.DeleteSyncValueRuntimeArgs.html)- Sync - Value - Runtime - Args
- [Delete](https://docs.rs/struct.DeleteSyncValueRuntimeResult.html)- Sync - Value - Runtime - Result
- Result type for Delete command
- [Delete](https://docs.rs/struct.DeleteSyncValueRuntimes.html)- Sync - Value - Runtimes
- Command to delete multiple entities by ID
- [Delete](https://docs.rs/struct.DeleteSyncValueRuntimesArgs.html)- Sync - Value - Runtimes - Args
- [Delete](https://docs.rs/struct.DeleteSyncValueRuntimesResult.html)- Sync - Value - Runtimes - Result
- Result type for bulk Delete command
- [GetAll](https://docs.rs/struct.GetAllSyncValueRuntimes.html)- Sync - Value - Runtimes
- [GetSync](https://docs.rs/struct.GetSyncValueRuntimeById.html)- Value - Runtime - ById
- [GetSync](https://docs.rs/struct.GetSyncValueRuntimesByIds.html)- Value - Runtimes - ByIds
- [GetSync](https://docs.rs/struct.GetSyncValueRuntimesByQuery.html)- Value - Runtimes - ByQuery
- [Partial](https://docs.rs/struct.PartialSyncValueRuntime.html)- Sync - Value - Runtime
- Replicated runtime state for a sync value — one row per value `key`.
- [Search](https://docs.rs/struct.SearchSyncValueRuntime.html)- Sync - Value - Runtime
- Search this entity type by query string. Backed by the typed
per-entity `SearchIndex<T>`(exact + nucleo subsequence + Levenshtein typo). Returns matching ids in tier order.
- [Search](https://docs.rs/struct.SearchSyncValueRuntimeResult.html)- Sync - Value - Runtime - Result
- [Sync](https://docs.rs/struct.SyncValueRuntime.html)- Value - Runtime
- Replicated runtime state for a sync value — one row per value `key`.
- [Sync](https://docs.rs/struct.SyncValueRuntimeCount.html)- Value - Runtime - Count
- [Sync](https://docs.rs/struct.SyncValueRuntimeId.html)- Value - Runtime - Id

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Sync](https://docs.rs/enum.SyncValueRunningState.html)- Value - Running - State
- Running state of a sync value. Encoded explicitly (vs. a bool) so the TS type-export reads cleanly in UI code.

# rship_sync::value_runner - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/rship-sync/4.0.0-canary.64/rship_sync/value_runner/index.html

## Expand description

Lock-free value runner using hyphae cells.

Each SyncValue has a dedicated runner that:

- Receives ticks from the registry’s batch updater
- Applies rate-based value changes using pure atomics
- Exposes a cell for subscribers to watch

This implementation is fully lock-free with zero per-tick allocations.

[§](https://docs.rs#shared-timing)Shared Timing

All values sampled at the same rate share the same interval timer, ensuring synchronized updates across different values.

[§](https://docs.rs#manual-cleanup)Manual Cleanup

Runners are explicitly removed via `DestroySyncValue`. The registry
holds strong references so runners stay alive between create and destroy.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Value](https://docs.rs/struct.ValueRunner.html)- Runner
- Runner for a single synchronized value.
- [Value](https://docs.rs/struct.ValueRunnerRegistry.html)- Runner - Registry
- A collection of value runners sharing a single clock.
- [Value](https://docs.rs/struct.ValueUpdate.html)- Update
- A value update emitted to subscribers.

# smooai-smooth-operator-server

The **reference WebSocket service** for [smooth-operator](https://github.com/SmooAI/smooth-operator) — the deployment surface.

It speaks the schema-driven protocol in [ spec/](https://github.com/SmooAI/smooth-operator/tree/main/spec) over a smooth-operator-backed

`KnowledgeChatRuntime`, so the generated TypeScript / Python / Go / .NET / Rust clients connect and drive real LLM turns unmodified. Run it locally with `cargo run -p smooai-smooth-operator-server` (in-memory storage, no database to provision), or deploy it three ways from the one codebase:- **Local**—- `cargo run`, in-memory adapter, for development and the cross-language E2E.
- **Kubernetes**— Helm + ArgoCD, Postgres + pgvector, the Redis/NATS backplane for multi-pod scale-out.
- **AWS serverless (SST)**— the companion- `smooth-operator-lambda`

See [ docs/DEPLOY.md](https://github.com/SmooAI/smooth-operator/blob/main/docs/DEPLOY.md) for the full matrix.

Part of the ** smooth-operator** service — Smoo AI's polyglot AI agent service (one schema-driven WebSocket protocol, five native clients, AWS-serverless or Kubernetes deploy). See the

[repository](https://github.com/SmooAI/smooth-operator)for the architecture, protocol, and the other crates.

# anyhow - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/anyhow/^1/

## Expand description

This library provides [ anyhow::Error](https://docs.rs/struct.Error.html), a trait object based error
type for easy idiomatic error handling in Rust applications.

[§](https://docs.rs#details)Details

-
Use `Result<T, anyhow::Error>`, or equivalently`anyhow::Result<T>`, as the return type of any fallible function.Within the function, use `?`to easily propagate any error that implements the`std::error::Error``use anyhow::Result; fn get_cluster_info() -> Result<ClusterMap> { let config = std::fs::read_to_string("cluster.json")?; let map: ClusterMap = serde_json::from_str(&config)?; Ok(map) }`
-
Attach context to help the person troubleshooting the error understand where things went wrong. A low-level error like “No such file or directory” can be annoying to debug without more context about what higher level step the application was in the middle of. `use anyhow::{Context, Result}; fn main() -> Result<()> { ... it.detach().context("Failed to detach the important thing")?; let content = std::fs::read(path) .with_context(|| format!("Failed to read instrs from {}", path))?; ... }``Error: Failed to read instrs from ./path/to/instrs.json Caused by: No such file or directory (os error 2)`
-
Downcasting is supported and can be by value, by shared reference, or by mutable reference as needed. `// If the error was caused by redaction, then return a // tombstone instead of the content. match root_cause.downcast_ref::<DataStoreError>() { Some(DataStoreError::Censored(_)) => Ok(Poll::Ready(REDACTED_CONTENT)), None => Err(error), }`
-
If using Rust ≥ 1.65, a backtrace is captured and printed with the error if the underlying error type does not already provide its own. In order to see backtraces, they must be enabled through the environment variables described in `std::backtrace`- If you want panics and errors to both have backtraces, set
`RUST_BACKTRACE=1`;
- If you want only errors to have backtraces, set `RUST_LIB_BACKTRACE=1`;
- If you want only panics to have backtraces, set `RUST_BACKTRACE=1`and`RUST_LIB_BACKTRACE=0`.

- If you want panics and errors to both have backtraces, set
-
Anyhow works with any error type that has an impl of `std::error::Error`, including ones defined in your crate. We do not bundle a`derive(Error)`macro but you can write the impls yourself or use a standalone macro like[thiserror](https://github.com/dtolnay/thiserror).`use thiserror::Error; #[derive(Error, Debug)] pub enum FormatError { #[error("Invalid header (expected {expected:?}, got {found:?})")] InvalidHeader { expected: String, found: String, }, #[error("Missing attribute: {0}")] MissingAttribute(String), }`
-
One-off error messages can be constructed using the `anyhow!`macro, which supports string interpolation and produces an`anyhow::Error`.`return Err(anyhow!("Missing attribute: {}", missing));`A `bail!`macro is provided as a shorthand for the same early return.`bail!("Missing attribute: {}", missing);`

[§](https://docs.rs#no-std-support)No-std support

In no_std mode, almost all of the same API is available and works the same way. To depend on Anyhow in no_std mode, disable our default enabled “std” feature in Cargo.toml. A global allocator is required.

```
[dependencies]
anyhow = { version = "1.0", default-features = false }
```
With versions of Rust older than 1.81, no_std mode may require an additional
`.map_err(Error::msg)` when working with a non-Anyhow error type inside a
function that returns Anyhow’s error type, as the trait that `?`-based error
conversions are defined by is only available in std in those old versions.

## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use`- [anyhow](https://docs.rs/macro.anyhow.html)as format_err;

## Macros[§](https://docs.rs#macros)

- [anyhow](https://docs.rs/macro.anyhow.html)
- Construct an ad-hoc error from a string or existing non-`anyhow`error value.
- [bail](https://docs.rs/macro.bail.html)
- Return early with an error.
- [ensure](https://docs.rs/macro.ensure.html)
- Return early with an error if a condition is not satisfied.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Chain](https://docs.rs/struct.Chain.html)
- Iterator of a chain of source errors.
- [Error](https://docs.rs/struct.Error.html)
- The `Error`type, a wrapper around a dynamic error type.

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [Context](https://docs.rs/trait.Context.html)
- Provides the `context`method for`Result`.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [Ok](https://docs.rs/fn.Ok.html)
- Equivalent to `Ok::<_, anyhow::Error>(value)`.

## Type Aliases[§](https://docs.rs#types)

- [Result](https://docs.rs/type.Result.html)
- `Result<T, Error>`
