public-key policy for `<smooth-agent-chat>` connections. Defaults to
[ PermissiveWidgetAuth](https://docs.rs/smooai-smooth-operator/1.11.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/smooth_operator/widget_auth/struct.PermissiveWidgetAuth.html) (no enforcement) until a host installs a real
provider via

[.](https://docs.rs/struct.AppState.html#method.with_widget_auth)

`with_widget_auth`[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.agent_config)

`agent_config: `[Arc](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/sync/struct.Arc.html)<dyn [AgentConfigResolver](https://docs.rs/smooai-smooth-operator/1.11.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/smooth_operator/agent_config/trait.AgentConfigResolver.html)>**Per-agent behavior config hook.** Resolves an agent’s `instructions`
(system prompt), `personality`, `greeting`, and `conversation_workflow`
from its `agent_id` so a public chat agent behaves as its owner configured
— not as the generic org-default persona. Defaults to
[ StaticAgentConfigResolver](https://docs.rs/smooai-smooth-operator/1.11.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/smooth_operator/agent_config/struct.StaticAgentConfigResolver.html) (empty ⇒ no
per-agent config → the org default persona is used, unchanged); a host
installs a real provider (backed by the monorepo

`agents` table) via
[.](https://docs.rs/struct.AppState.html#method.with_agent_config)

`with_agent_config`[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.backplane)

`backplane: `[Arc](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/sync/struct.Arc.html)<dyn [Backplane](https://docs.rs/smooai-smooth-operator/1.11.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/smooth_operator/backplane/trait.Backplane.html)>Connection backplane: per-pod sink registry + cross-pod event delivery.
Defaults to [ InMemoryBackplane](https://docs.rs/smooai-smooth-operator/1.11.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/smooth_operator/backplane/struct.InMemoryBackplane.html) (single-process); a host installs a
Redis/NATS impl via

[to scale out and to let non-AI publishers push realtime events to connected clients.](https://docs.rs/struct.AppState.html#method.with_backplane)

`with_backplane`[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.chat_provider)

`chat_provider: `[Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[Arc](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/sync/struct.Arc.html)<dyn [LlmProvider](https://docs.rs/smooai-smooth-operator-core/0.15.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/smooth_operator_core/llm_provider/trait.LlmProvider.html)>>Test-only injected LLM surface. When `Some`, every `send_message` turn
runs the engine against this provider (a
[ MockLlmClient](https://docs.rs/smooai-smooth-operator-core/0.15.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/smooth_operator_core/llm_provider/struct.MockLlmClient.html))
instead of building a live gateway client from

`config` — exactly the
`ServerState(chat_client=mock)` seam the Python reference uses to drive the
scenario-parity corpus deterministically offline. **(a live client is built from the gateway config), so the**

`None` in production`/ws` path is
byte-for-byte unchanged for real deployments. Installed via
[.](https://docs.rs/struct.AppState.html#method.with_chat_provider)

`with_chat_provider`[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.gateway_key_resolver)

`gateway_key_resolver: `[Arc](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/sync/struct.Arc.html)<dyn [GatewayKeyResolver](https://docs.rs/smooai-smooth-operator/1.11.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/smooth_operator/gateway_key/trait.GatewayKeyResolver.html)>Per-org LLM gateway-key resolver: maps a turn’s `org_id` to the gateway
key it should bill/scope to. Defaults to [ EnvGatewayKeyResolver](https://docs.rs/smooai-smooth-operator/1.11.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/smooth_operator/gateway_key/struct.EnvGatewayKeyResolver.html) (the
single

`SMOOAI_GATEWAY_KEY` for every org — unchanged local behavior); a
multi-tenant host installs a per-org resolver via
[so each tenant’s usage is attributed to its own key. The per-turn LLM-config build falls back to the env key whenever the resolver returns](https://docs.rs/struct.AppState.html#method.with_gateway_key_resolver)

`with_gateway_key_resolver``None`.[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.otp_service)

`otp_service: `[Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[Arc](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/sync/struct.Arc.html)<dyn [OtpService](https://docs.rs/smooai-smooth-operator/1.11.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/smooth_operator/otp/trait.OtpService.html)>>**End-user OTP identity-verification seam.** When `Some`, a turn whose
auth gate refuses an `end_user` tool on an unverified session triggers the
OTP flow: the server emits `otp_verification_required`, calls
[ send_otp](https://docs.rs/smooai-smooth-operator/1.11.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/smooth_operator/otp/trait.OtpService.html#tymethod.send_otp), and emits

`otp_sent`; a later `verify_otp` action calls
[and, on success, marks the session authenticated.](https://docs.rs/smooai-smooth-operator/1.11.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/smooth_operator/otp/trait.OtpService.html#tymethod.verify_otp)

`verify_otp``None` (the default) keeps the
current fail-closed behavior — the `end_user` tool is refused and no OTP is
offered. Installed via [. The reference server never holds a code; the host owns generation/expiry.](https://docs.rs/struct.AppState.html#method.with_otp_service)

`with_otp_service`[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.shutdown)

`shutdown: `[CancellationToken](https://docs.rs/tokio-util/0.7.18/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/tokio_util/sync/cancellation_token/struct.CancellationToken.html)Graceful-shutdown signal, shared across every per-connection clone of this
state. On SIGTERM/ctrl_c the serve loop cancels this token; each
connection’s reader loop selects on [ CancellationToken::cancelled](https://docs.rs/tokio-util/0.7.18/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/tokio_util/sync/cancellation_token/struct.CancellationToken.html#method.cancelled) so it
finishes its in-flight turn, exits, and detaches from the

[— no in-flight turn dropped, no stale registry entry left behind. A fresh token from](https://docs.rs/smooai-smooth-operator/1.11.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/smooth_operator/backplane/trait.Backplane.html)

`Backplane`[is never cancelled, so the](https://docs.rs/struct.AppState.html#method.new)

`new``/ws` path and
tests are unaffected until a `run`/serve path wires the signal.[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.serve_widget)

`serve_widget: `[bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)When `true`, the router mounts the embedded widget host page at `/` and
the widget bundle at `/chat-widget.iife.js`. Off by default (the
K8s/Lambda flavors never serve the widget); the local flavor opts in via
[ with_widget](https://docs.rs/struct.AppState.html#method.with_widget).

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.widget_token)

`widget_token: `[Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)>The auth token injected into the served widget host page (same-origin), so
the embedded widget connects to this server’s `/ws?token=…`. `None` ⇒ no
token injected (a no-auth local server).

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.strict_auth)

`strict_auth: `[bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)**Strict auth.** When `true`, the `/ws` connect path **rejects** a
missing/invalid token (HTTP 401) instead of degrading to an anonymous
connection. Off by default (K8s/widget anonymous flows unchanged); a
single-tenant local/tailnet deployment opts in via
[ with_strict_auth](https://docs.rs/struct.AppState.html#method.with_strict_auth) so a tokenless peer can’t
drive the agent.

[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.default_persona)

`default_persona: `[Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)>**Default agent persona / system prompt.** When `Some`, it is used as the
turn’s system prompt whenever the per-org [`AgentSettings::persona`] is
`None` — i.e. a host-supplied default that replaces the built-in
customer-support [ KNOWLEDGE_CHAT_SYSTEM_PROMPT](https://docs.rs/runner/index.html) when no
per-org override exists. The single-tenant local daemon installs its
“Big Smooth” personal-assistant persona here via

[.](https://docs.rs/struct.AppState.html#method.with_default_persona)

`with_default_persona``None` (the default)
keeps the const prompt, so the cloud flavor is byte-for-byte unchanged.[§](https://docs.rs#structfield.model_costs_cache)

`model_costs_cache: `[Arc](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/sync/struct.Arc.html)<[OnceCell](https://docs.rs/tokio/1.52.3/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/tokio/sync/once_cell/struct.OnceCell.html)<[Value](https://docs.rs/serde_json/1.0.150/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/serde_json/value/enum.Value.html)>>**Model-pricing cache** for `GET /admin/model-costs`. The gateway’s
`/v1/model/info` pricing is stable, so it’s fetched at most once per
process and reused for every subsequent request (the admin handler sets
this on the first successful fetch; a gateway error is NOT cached, so a
transient failure is retried on the next request). Shared across clones so
every connection/request sees the same cached map.

installs a resolver backed by its per-org key store (e.g. one LiteLLM
virtual key per tenant) so each org’s turns are billed/scoped to its own
key. The per-turn LLM-config build falls back to the env key whenever the
resolver returns `None`, so a resolver covering only some orgs is safe.
Leaving this unset keeps the default [ EnvGatewayKeyResolver](https://docs.rs/smooai-smooth-operator/1.11.1/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/smooth_operator/gateway_key/struct.EnvGatewayKeyResolver.html) (single env
key for every org — unchanged local behavior).

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/smooth_operator_server/state.rs.html#374-377)

Install the end-user OTP identity-verification service (builder). Wires the
`end_user` auth gate to an OTP flow (see [ otp_service](https://docs.rs/struct.AppState.html#structfield.otp_service));
leaving it unset keeps the fail-closed default (refuse, no OTP offered).

Install the graceful-shutdown signal (builder). The serve loop owns a
clone of this token and cancels it on SIGTERM/ctrl_c; every per-connection
clone observes the cancellation and drains. Defaulted to a fresh token in
[ new](https://docs.rs/struct.AppState.html#method.new), so this is only needed when a caller wants to drive
shutdown from its own token.

The caller’s OTP contact points for this session, read from the session’s
`metadata.contactEmail` / `metadata.contactPhone` (stashed at
create-session time). Empty when the session is unknown or captured no

path captures only an email.

Record that a document was added to a named document set **within an org**
(increments its count). Used by seeding + the ingest path so
`GET /admin/document-sets` can report set names + counts despite the
in-memory backend dropping document metadata. Org-scoped so org A’s sets
are never reported to an org-B caller.

Snapshot **one org’s** document-set registry as `(name, count)` pairs,
sorted by name for a stable response. Never returns another org’s sets.

Record a connector (within an org) whose indexing runs should be listed
(idempotent). Org-scoped so a same-named connector in two orgs records
separately and `GET /admin/indexing/runs` only lists the caller’s org’s.

Take (remove + return) the pending [ HumanResponse](https://docs.rs/smooai-smooth-operator-core/0.15.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/smooth_operator_core/human/enum.HumanResponse.html) sender for

`session_id`, if a turn is parked on a confirmation. Returns `None` when

Drop any pending confirmation registered for `session_id` without
resolving it. Called when a parked turn ends (the bridge task finishes)
so a stale sender can’t linger and mis-route a later confirmation.

# smooth_operator_server::handler - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/smooai-smooth-operator-server/1.11.1/smooth_operator_server/handler/index.html

## Expand description

Action dispatch — parses a client action envelope and produces the matching server events.

Each handler is `async` and forwards events through an
`UnboundedSender<serde_json::Value>` (the per-connection outbound sink). The
socket task drains the sink and writes each value as a JSON WS text frame, so
streaming actions (`send_message`) can emit many events while still being
driven from one place.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [handle_](https://docs.rs/fn.handle_frame.html)- frame
- Parse and dispatch a single inbound text frame. Any produced events are sent
through `sink`. Returns`Ok(())`always — protocol-level failures are surfaced as`error`events, never as hard errors that drop the connection.

---

# smooth_operator_server::runner - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/smooai-smooth-operator-server/1.11.1/smooth_operator_server/runner/index.html

## Expand description

The streaming, memory-carrying agent runner used by the WS service.

`smooth-operator`’s [`KnowledgeChatRuntime`] proves the engine ↔ gateway
path but (a) is non-streaming (`run_turn` returns only after the turn
completes) and (b) has no cross-turn memory — each `run_turn` builds a fresh
[ Agent](https://docs.rs/smooai-smooth-operator-core/0.15.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/smooth_operator_core/agent/struct.Agent.html) with a random id and no prior messages, so turn 2 forgets turn 1
(documented in

`core/tests/e2e_llm_smoo_ai.rs`).The service needs both, so this module builds the agent itself, wiring the same knowledge-grounding as core PLUS:

- **Streaming**via- `Agent::run_with_channel`- `AgentEvent`- `stream_token`,- `stream_chunk`,- `eventual_response`).
- **Per-session memory**via- `AgentConfig::with_prior_messages`- `Agent::new`randomizes the agent id every time, so the checkpoint-resume path can’t be keyed stably — replaying the persisted log is the robust, backend-agnostic way to carry memory. The log is the source of truth the adapter already persists.)

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Confirmation](https://docs.rs/struct.ConfirmationConfig.html)- Config
- Hooks the runner needs to wire **write-confirmation HITL**into a turn without depending on`AppState`directly (keeps the runner unit-testable).
- [Turn](https://docs.rs/struct.TurnRequest.html)- Request
- Everything one streaming turn needs. Bundled into a struct so the call sites
(the reference server’s `handle_send_message`and the lambda’s`send_message`) stay readable and the security-critical`access`
- [Turn](https://docs.rs/struct.TurnResult.html)- Result
- The terminal outcome of a streamed turn.
- [Workflow](https://docs.rs/struct.WorkflowTurn.html)- Turn
- A turn’s **conversation-workflow**context: the agent’s configured workflow plus the step the conversation is currently on. When present on a`TurnRequest``None`(the default) means the agent runs freeform — no workflow section, no judge, byte-for-byte unchanged.

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [general_](https://docs.rs/fn.general_agent_response.html)- agent_ - response
- Build the structured `GeneralAgentResponse`-shaped payload the protocol’s`eventual_response`carries. The reference runtime doesn’t produce the full structured analytics, so we surface the reply text in`responseParts`and supply neutral defaults for the analytic fields (clients render`responseParts`).
- [run_](https://docs.rs/fn.run_streaming_turn.html)- streaming_ - turn
- Runs one knowledge-grounded, streaming turn for a session’s conversation and
emits protocol-shaped events through `sink`as they happen.

## Type Aliases[§](https://docs.rs#types)

- [Clear](https://docs.rs/type.ClearConfirmation.html)- Confirmation
- Clears any registered confirmation sender for a session id when its turn ends.
Typically `AppState::clear_confirmation`.
- [Register](https://docs.rs/type.RegisterConfirmation.html)- Confirmation
- Registers a parked turn’s `HumanResponse``confirm_tool_action`can take it). Typically`AppState::register_confirmation`.

---

Spawn a sub-agent to work on the given task in a background tokio task.

The sub-agent inherits the parent’s `LlmConfig`. If `sub_config.inherit_tools`
is true, the parent’s tool registry is cloned (tool `Arc`s are shared, hooks are not).

#### pub async fn [run_with_channel](https://docs.rs#method.run_with_channel)(
    &self,
    user_message: impl [Into](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/convert/trait.Into.html)<[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)>,
    tx: [UnboundedSender](https://docs.rs/tokio/1.52.3/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/tokio/sync/mpsc/unbounded/struct.UnboundedSender.html)<[AgentEvent](https://docs.rs/enum.AgentEvent.html)>,
) -> [Result](https://docs.rs/anyhow/1.0.103/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/anyhow/type.Result.html)<[Conversation](https://docs.rs/conversation/struct.Conversation.html)>

Run the agent loop with streaming LLM responses, sending events through a channel.

This is the streaming counterpart to `run()`. Instead of using the closure-based
event handler, all events (including token deltas) are sent through the provided
`mpsc::UnboundedSender`. This is designed for TUI consumption.

[§](https://docs.rs#errors-2)Errors

Returns error if the LLM call or tool execution fails fatally.

# smooth_operator_server::server - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/smooai-smooth-operator-server/1.11.1/smooth_operator_server/server/index.html

## Expand description

The axum WebSocket server: one `/ws` endpoint, one task per connection.

Per connection we split the socket and run two tasks joined by an
`UnboundedSender<serde_json::Value>` outbound sink:

- a **writer**that drains the sink and writes each event as a JSON text frame, and
- a **reader**that reads inbound frames and dispatches them via`crate::handler::handle_frame``send_message`) can emit events as they happen.

Using a sink channel (instead of writing directly from the handler) is what
lets a streaming turn fire many `stream_token` events from inside the agent
loop while the connection is still reading.

## Constants[§](https://docs.rs#constants)

- [SEED_](https://docs.rs/constant.SEED_ORG_ID.html)- ORG_ - ID
- The org the seeded demo docs + their document-set registry entries belong to.
Mirrors the org `handler::handle_create_session`stamps onto reference conversations, so the seeded sets show up for the reference org’s admin caller (and ONLY that org — cross-org scoping).

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [bind](https://docs.rs/fn.bind.html)
- Bind on `<SMOOTH_AGENT_BIND>:<port>`(default loopback) and serve until the process is killed. Returns the bound`TcpListener`
- [build_](https://docs.rs/fn.build_state.html)- state
- Build an `AppState``config.seed_kb`is set. Exposed for tests + the binary.
- [build_](https://docs.rs/fn.build_state_from_env.html)- state_ - from_ - env
- Build an `AppState`**env-configured**auth verifier (secure by default — see`smooth_operator::auth::AuthConfig`
- [build_](https://docs.rs/fn.build_state_from_env_async.html)- state_ - from_ - env_ - async
- Build an `AppState`**storage backend**(and the matching durable**admin stores**) from`config.storage`, then installing the env-configured auth verifier.
- [router](https://docs.rs/fn.router.html)
- Build the axum `Router``/ws`endpoint plus the auth-gated admin HTTP API under`/admin`(see`crate::admin`
- [run](https://docs.rs/fn.run.html)
- Run the server to completion (blocks). Logs a single listening line.
- [seed_](https://docs.rs/fn.seed_knowledge.html)- knowledge
- Seed a couple of distinctive demo docs so knowledge-grounded E2E is
deterministic. The 17-day return window is deliberately unusual so an
ungrounded answer can’t accidentally match it. Both docs are tagged into the
`policies`document set so the admin API can report it.
- [serve_](https://docs.rs/fn.serve_state.html)- state
- Serve a **pre-built**`AppState``state.config.bind:state.config.port`.
- [serve_](https://docs.rs/fn.serve_state_on.html)- state_ - on
- Serve a pre-built `AppState``TcpListener`

# bind in smooth_operator_server::server - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/smooai-smooth-operator-server/1.11.1/smooth_operator_server/server/fn.bind.html

```
pub async fn bind(
    config:
```
[ServerConfig](https://docs.rs/config/struct.ServerConfig.html),
) -> [Result](https://docs.rs/anyhow/1.0.102/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/anyhow/type.Result.html)<([TcpListener](https://docs.rs/tokio/1.52.3/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/tokio/net/tcp/listener/struct.TcpListener.html), [Router](https://docs.rs/axum/0.8.9/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/axum/routing/struct.Router.html), [CancellationToken](https://docs.rs/tokio-util/0.7.18/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/tokio_util/sync/cancellation_token/struct.CancellationToken.html))>## Expand description

Bind on `<SMOOTH_AGENT_BIND>:<port>` (default loopback) and serve until the
process is killed. Returns the bound [ TcpListener](https://docs.rs/tokio/1.52.3/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/tokio/net/tcp/listener/struct.TcpListener.html) + the router, used by
both the binary and tests (tests bind port 0 for an ephemeral port).

Uses the **env-configured, secure-by-default** auth verifier
([ build_state_from_env](https://docs.rs/fn.build_state_from_env.html)) — the binary refuses to start if auth is
misconfigured rather than silently serving the admin API unauthenticated.

[§](https://docs.rs#errors)Errors

Returns an error if the auth configuration is invalid or the TCP bind fails.

# smooth_operator_server::local - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/smooai-smooth-operator-server/1.11.1/smooth_operator_server/local/index.html

## Expand description

The **local deployment flavor** — an embeddable, zero-config server.

This is the third deployment target alongside `deploy/k8s` (Kubernetes +
Postgres + NATS) and `deploy/sst` (AWS serverless): a self-contained server
with **everything in-memory** and **auth off**, meant to run on a developer
laptop or to be **embedded in-process** by a host (e.g. the smooth daemon).

It needs no external services — no Postgres, no Redis, no NATS, no AWS — and
no secrets. It is exactly the default-flavor server the binary already boots
when no env is set ([ ServerConfig::from_env](https://docs.rs/config/struct.ServerConfig.html#method.from_env)
defaults to in-memory storage, in-memory backplane, loopback bind, and admin
disabled), factored here so a host can boot it from code in a few lines
rather than by shelling out and setting env vars.

[§](https://docs.rs#in-process-embed)In-process embed

```
// Boot a fully in-memory server on the default loopback addr, in the
// background, and get a handle to its real bound address + a shutdown switch.
let server = smooth_operator_server::local::LocalServer::builder()
    .seed_kb(true) // optional: load the demo knowledge docs
    .spawn()
    .await?;
println!("local operator on ws://{}/ws", server.addr());
// ... use it (connect a client, run turns) ...
server.shutdown().await; // graceful stop + join
```
[§](https://docs.rs#run-to-completion)Run to completion

```
// Or just run it in the foreground until killed (what the binary's no-env
// path effectively does):
smooth_operator_server::local::serve_local("127.0.0.1:8787").await?;
```
[§](https://docs.rs#what-local-flavor-pins)What “local flavor” pins

Independent of ambient env, the local flavor always uses:

- **storage**= in-memory (- `InMemoryStorageAdapter`
- **backplane**= in-memory (single-process; no Redis/NATS),
- **auth**= none (- `NoAuthVerifier`- `/admin`is open,- `/ws`boots,
- **widget auth**= permissive (- `PermissiveWidgetAuth`
- **bind**= a caller-supplied addr (default- `127.0.0.1:8787`).

The LLM gateway is still read from `SMOOAI_GATEWAY_URL` / `SMOOAI_GATEWAY_KEY`
(so a key in the environment enables live turns); with no key, `send_message`
returns a clean protocol `error` exactly as the keyless test path does.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Local](https://docs.rs/struct.LocalServer.html)- Server
- A running [local-flavor](https://docs.rs/index.html)server: its bound address + a graceful shutdown switch.
- [Local](https://docs.rs/struct.LocalServerBuilder.html)- Server - Builder
- Builder for the [local deployment flavor](https://docs.rs/index.html): a fully in-memory, auth-off, single-process server, embeddable in-process.

## Constants[§](https://docs.rs#constants)

- [DEFAULT_](https://docs.rs/constant.DEFAULT_LOCAL_ADDR.html)- LOCAL_ - ADDR
- The default address the local flavor binds when the caller gives none —
loopback on the canonical WebSocket port, matching
`config::DEFAULT_BIND``config::DEFAULT_PORT`

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [local_](https://docs.rs/fn.local_config.html)- config
- An `ServerConfig`**in-memory storage**pinned. The gateway URL/key are still read from the environment via`ServerConfig::from_env``send_message`errors cleanly.
- [serve_](https://docs.rs/fn.serve_local.html)- local
- Run a [local-flavor](https://docs.rs/index.html)server to completion (blocks) on`addr`.

# serve_local in smooth_operator_server::local - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/smooai-smooth-operator-server/1.11.1/smooth_operator_server/local/fn.serve_local.html

## Expand description

Run a [local-flavor](https://docs.rs/index.html) server to completion (blocks) on `addr`.

Convenience for the foreground / one-command case: boots a fully in-memory,
auth-off server bound to `addr` and serves until the process is killed. For
an embedded server you can stop programmatically, use
[ LocalServer::builder](https://docs.rs/struct.LocalServer.html#method.builder) +

[instead.](https://docs.rs/struct.LocalServer.html#method.shutdown)

`LocalServer::shutdown`[§](https://docs.rs#errors)Errors

Returns an error if `addr` doesn’t parse, the bind fails, or serving fails.
